verdict: REVISE. Independently rebuilt and reran everything. Round 1 (MSBuild/DTB mechanism) reproduced in full: removing MyriadSdkGenerateCode's DesignTimeBuild gate makes Myriad's real <Exec> run during a genuine DTB (SkipCompilerExecution=true), regenerating a changed record's lens on disk with the compiler never running (bin/*.dll mtime frozen under a moved canary), and the existing rebuild cache still correctly no-ops an unchanged repeat DTB and re-fires on a real change. Round 2a (cold FSAC 0.83.0 over real hand-rolled LSP) reproduced both directions: scratch-ungated's generated file went Name-only -> Name+Age purely from FSAC's cold workspaceLoad and hover on Age RESOLVED with real type info, zero dotnet build; scratch-gated negative control correctly returned NULL for Age (Name resolving proves it's a real discrimination, not a broken fixture). First real-LSP-process 'works live' test in this repo's lineage and it holds. Round 2b-2e (live edit, no restart) reproduced as reported for the four signals the executor tried (source didChange/didSave, didChangeWatchedFiles on source, second workspaceLoad, didChangeWatchedFiles-notification on the .fsproj) - all leave the canary frozen and Email unresolved. BUT the results doc's sharpest negative ('there may be no way to reload a running FSAC session short of restarting the language server') is falsified: I actually mutated the .fsproj on disk (even a bare File.SetLastWriteTimeUtc mtime touch, no content change, no notification) then reissued workspaceLoad in the same running process, and codegen re-ran live - canary moved, Email lens written, hover RESOLVED, no restart. FSAC/Ionide.ProjInfo caches the cracked project keyed on .fsproj mtime; the executor's 2e only notified of a change without changing the file, so the cache correctly short-circuited. Corrected, the result lands exactly on the design's pre-registered REVISE wording: closes the gap at project-(re)load time only, not during live source editing. This does not rescue the practical capability - a developer adding a field to a .fs file does not change the .fsproj, so a bare source save still never re-runs codegen; the correction changes the mechanism story (in-session reload IS possible via the ordinary project-reload path), not the capability ceiling. Also confirmed: --adaptive-lsp-server-enabled changes nothing (cold works, live 2b-2e still fail); no real dotnet build ran in any session (bin dlls frozen). Fixture is fair (diff vs real Myriad.Sdk.targets = only the gate removal, canary Touch, dropped empty DTB no-op). No contradiction with Q006 (Thread-1-shaped: Myriad writes a real .fs to disk before CoreCompile, compiled as ordinary source; no provider resolves an in-progress type). Caveats: one record, Lenses only (Fields named but never exercised), one machine, FSAC 0.83.0, fsautocomplete-directly not the VS Code+Ionide UI, and lsp-client logs are overwrite-mode so the executor's original logs were overwritten by reruns (pattern corroborated by my own independent reruns). Amendment required to 02-results.md: strike the 'only a restart works' sentence in 'What actually happened vs. what the design predicted'.
